How we calculate the comparison

For one year, reports per 100,000 residents = filtered reports ÷ that state’s population in the same year × 100,000. For All years, we calculate each annual rate first, then take their arithmetic mean. Each active year has equal weight. An active year has at least one matching report and a population value; years with zero reports are not averaged.

The count ranking and scatter show reports per active year and mean population over those same active years. Tooltips and CSV include Active_Years_Count. A state with no active years has no average. This matches our group’s AVG of annual rates query.

Population rates use reports from 1900 onward with matching state-year populations. The supplied population data ends in 2024, so 2025–2026 reports have no denominator and cannot enter the rates.

Shape, month, local hour, media and search filters change the report count. The denominator remains the full population for the covered year or years. These filtered rates describe self-reported accounts. Population alone cannot establish what caused a sighting or a report.

Population source is the group-supplied State_Population.json, covering years through 2024. Our group sourced the population series from Rolf Hendriks’s compilation of U.S. Census Bureau data on Kaggle. Washington, DC is mapped by its full name. We keep missing populations unavailable, with no interpolation or use of another year.

The state comparison and its CSV cover the 50 states and Washington, DC. Territory reports remain in the report explorer. The CSV includes unmatched states with an empty population and rate, and a coverage status.

Original source accounts

These are self-reported observations in a selected sample. They are not verified extraterrestrial events.
